label: Trapezoid Pocket
description: The trapezoid chest pocket cuts its welt with converging edges. The welt stands deepest at its outboard end, the end nearest the armhole, and narrows steadily as it runs inboard toward the centre front, so its top and bottom edges close gently toward one another along the length of the run. Which end carries the depth is the whole point of the option: the deep end is the armhole side, the shallow end the centre-front side. The taper is restrained rather than dramatic, roughly a seventh deeper at the outboard end than at the inboard one, and it is that gentle convergence along the run that must read in the photograph. The opening is left completely empty so both edges are visible along their full length and the direction of the taper is unmistakable. It is an uncommon cut, a quiet signature for tailors who enjoy subverting conventional geometry.

garment.fabric: fine wool suiting with visible weave
